charts.name: Papua New Guinea reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in the texts read for Papua New Guinea, and no text read names a standard setter or a framework for company accounts. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-style statements below (IAS 1, expenses by nature), with the accounts a Papua New Guinea trading company keeps — GST output and input tax, import GST owed to Customs, salary and wages tax withheld, superannuation contributions and withholding taxes payable.

numbering.legal_reference: No text read states the content of a tax invoice or a numbering rule. `sequential` and the number format are conventions of this pack and not rules of the law.

tax_point.legal_reference: No text read states when GST becomes due on a supply (the Goods and Services Tax Act 2003 itself could not be opened: PacLII and the IRC site refuse automated reads). `invoice_date` is the pack's simplification and not a finding of the law; the point of the tax is a gap recorded in the README.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No structured e-invoice standard, Peppol profile or clearance system of the Internal Revenue Commission was found in the texts read; the GST return is the paper or spreadsheet form G1. `obligation` is `none` for want of a text, not on a finding that none exists.

not_taxed.legal_reference: The guide read says the legislation contains reverse charge provisions for certain supplies made to a resident from outside Papua New Guinea, but neither the G1 form nor the fact sheet gives a line for it. The pack therefore carries no purchase tax for services bought from abroad. This is a finding about the texts read, not a finding that no reverse charge exists: it is a gap recorded in the README.
